text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- The debate over NATO's expansion into former Soviet bloc is postponed for time being out of consideration for Moscow. Kohl, Cointon, chirac and Kajor agree on this.
- U.S. general consulate in Stuttgart is to be closed down.
- Opposition Social Democrat (SPD) majority in Bundesrat upper house of parliament look likely to reject government's austerity measures.
- Premier of North Rhine-Westphalia Johannes Rau opens huge American-style shopping mall in Oberhausen.
- Building trade cuts sick pay from November. Demands for cut in wage for 13th month.
- BDI industry federation says industrial balance between east and west Germany will take 15 to 20 years.
- HDE retailers union says that 10 to 15 percent of shops will stay open longer after new law on shop closing hours comes into effect. No boost is expected to sales or employment.
HANDELSBLATT
- Row between Labour Miniser Norbert Bluem and Finance Minister Theo Waigel over government cuts to Labour Office budget as part of government's austerity measures.
- Kohl defends his savings programme in Bundestag lower house of parliament.
- Centro -- a huge american-style shopping mall in north western Germany -- waiting for the masses.
- BDI German industry federation says that east Germany needs at least 15 to 20 years to catch up with west Germany.
- Ifo economic research institute says that further interest rate cuts are not expected this year.
- Dollar continues is upward trend in European forex market.
- Hans Peter Stihl, president of the German Trade and Industry Congress, said he expected important economic impuses from Kohl's seven-day trip to Latin America starting Saturday.
- HDE retailers trade union says new shop opening times that come into effect in November will mean that only 10 to 15 percent of shops will take advantage of longer shop hours.

- Bonn coalition does not majority support among population according to a survey by Forsa institute. It said that Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) along with its Bavarian sister party the Christian Social Union (CSU) had 39 percent and the Free Democrats (FDP') junior coalition partner had seven percent.
- Kohl wants German-Czech declaration by end of 1996
- German President Roman Herzog supports Slovenia's NATO membership.
- Over a billion pounds in bonus for Reuters shareholders.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG

- Kohl says he's making no compromises over his austerity programme. In the budget debate in the Bundestag lower house of parliament Chancellor Kohl offer opposition Social Democrats (SPD) and the trade unions a renewed dialogue over his savings plans. SPd leader Oscar Lafontaine accuses government of social injustice.
- Construction employers want to cut sick pay.
- Every second shop tests the new shop hours.
DIE WELT
- Kohl defends his austerity programme. Oskar Lafontaine rejects Kohl's offer to work together on second day of budget debate.
- Minor earthquake in eastern Germany.
- Allensbach institute survey says Kohl's CDU/CSU union lacks majority among voters with 37 percent. Junior coalition partner has 7.8 percent.
- New resistance against a minimum wage. Workers from the textile and metal industry opposed to generally binding pay levels.
